title: Countersunk angle bracket
prompt: Angle bracket: an L seen from the side, 50 mm along the floor and 40 mm tall, 5 mm thick, 40 mm wide, with a 4 mm radius fillet in the inside corner. Two countersunk holes for M4 flat-head screws (ISO 10642) in each leg, 20 mm apart across the width: in the floor leg 30 mm out from the back, in the upright 25 mm up from the floor, countersunk on the inside faces. Put the outside corner edge along the Y axis (back face on X = 0, bottom on Z = 0), centred on Y = 0, with the floor leg going +X. Make them countersunk hole features with the M4 preset.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
Back on X = 0, bottom on Z = 0, centred on Y
Four M4 countersunk holes: Ø4.5 clearance, ISO 10642 countersink Ø9.18 × 90°
Countersunk from the inside faces: the floor holes open at x = 30 on the shelf (z = 5), the upright holes at z = 25 on the inner face (x = 5), 20 mm apart
R4 inside-corner fillet adds (1 − π/4)·16·40 = 137.3 mm³: volume 16611 mm³ ±0.3%

notes: L area 425 mm² × 40 = 17000, + concave R4 fillet 137.35, − 4 countersunk through holes of 131.64 each (cone depth (9.18 − 4.5)/2 = 2.34) = 16610.8 mm³. Construction: csinks reads the hole features the prompt asks for (no geometry equivalent in the report), so a correct part built otherwise fails only that test.
